conviction_note: The findings offset to a sum of 0.0. A crowded and rising short (17.1% of float, 9.7 days to cover) on a stock 54% off its high argues up. Against that: a loss ratio that may look worse year on year once the 7-point favourable reserve release in Q2 does not repeat, a heavier personal-lines catastrophe quarter in the industry, and a name that sold its last three revenue beats. abs_move is 15, above the 13.3 implied move, because the history median is 14.85 and the hunters have run small. p_up is 48: the put skew and three straight down reactions lean a little negative, and the squeeze risk stops it going lower.
bar: The company's own Q3 2026 guide from the Q2 letter (2026-07-29): in-force premium $1,537-1,540M, gross earned premium $356-359M, revenue $323-326M, adjusted EBITDA -$23M to -$20M, stock comp $24M. FY2026 guide: in-force premium $1,632-1,639M, revenue $1,214-1,220M, adjusted EBITDA -$51M to -$47M, implying about +$8M adjusted EBITDA in Q4. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001691421/000169142126000047/lmndshareholderletterq22.htm. Street consensus: revenue $322.4M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/LMND/earnings-forecasts, seen only as a search snippet) and EPS -$0.60 across 6 analysts (therighttrader https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/lmnd and Benzinga agree). The bar is sourced to the company guide and to two agreeing estimate sources. Gross loss ratio is not guided; the Q2 call said it will be 'more of an output than an input'.
positioning_check: Short interest at the 2026-10-15 settlement was 11,625,163 shares, 17.11% of float, 9.65 days to cover, up 2.1% from 11,383,738 on 2026-09-30. It has risen from 9,984,175 on 2026-08-14 (MarketBeat from FINRA, published 2026-10-26: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LMND/short-interest/; series on Equibles: https://equibles.com/stocks/lmnd/short-interest). This is a crowded short. The baseline has 25-delta skew at +10.61 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest 0.68, an event-implied move of 13.31%, spot $44.80, 53.6% below the 52-week high and 8.8% above the low, with a 20-day run-up of -4.3%. Reactions to the last three prints were -6.2%, -14.9% and -23.7%; the November 2025 print was +34.2%.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded and rising into the print: 11.63M shares (17.1% of float, 9.65 days to cover) at 2026-10-15, up from 9.98M on 2026-08-14. The stock is $44.80, 53.6% below its 52-week high and about 18% below the $54.45-54.63 at which an insider's 10b5-1 sales filled on 2026-09-03/04. Any print that does not damage the Q4 positive-EBITDA target has a squeeze mechanism behind it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: With a double-digit short, the November 2025 print went +34.2% and August 2025 +29.5% (baseline). The last three prints went -6.2%, -14.9% and -23.7%, so the short has been paid on recent prints rather than squeezed.
findings.why_not_priced: The skew is +10.6 vol points to the downside and the stock sits near its 52-week low, so options price continuation, not a squeeze. If the squeeze were priced, the calls would carry the premium and short interest would be falling into the print, not rising.
findings.independence: Equibles shows the same FINRA series rising since August (https://equibles.com/stocks/lmnd/short-interest). The September insider sale prices come from the Form 4 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1691421/000181629926000023/xslF345X06/wk-form4_1788903193.xml (CIO John Peters, 10b5-1 and tax-withholding sales of 3,108 shares, not a signal in itself).

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 gross loss ratio of 60% included 7 points of favourable prior-period development. Excluding CAT and PPD, the attritional ratio rose to 59% from 54% in Q1 2026. Management called the gross loss ratio an 'output' it will let move to buy growth, and named vet-cost inflation in Pet. If PPD does not recur, the Q3 gross loss ratio can print in the low-to-mid 60s against 62% in Q3 2025: the first year-on-year deterioration headline in years, on a stock whose story is 'AI lowers the loss ratio'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (-23.7%) and Q1 2026 (-14.9%) both sold off on profitability and expense worries despite revenue beats (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/why-lemonade-stock-crashing-today). On loss-ratio improvement prints in 2025, the stock rose about 30% twice (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The headline 60% and the 7-point improvement year on year went out on the wire; the 59% attritional figure net of PPD sits in the body of the letter. Every 'loss ratio improved 11 points' headline from Q3 2025 sets the year-on-year comparison at 62%. Partly priced: the stock has fallen 24% since. Consensus is shaped on revenue and EPS, not the loss ratio.
findings.independence: Same document family as finding 3 (both bear on the loss ratio) but a different driver. The 'output not input' and vet-inflation remarks come from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1978055-20260808). Trupanion's Q3 preview says vet inflation is still in double digits (https://finviz.com/news/411055/trupanions-pet-growth-faces-a-test-as-guidance-points-to-slower-profit-gains).

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was a much heavier personal-lines catastrophe quarter than Q3 2025. Allstate reported $1.65bn of Q3 cat losses, nearly three times last year's $558M. Hippo's Q3 CAT loss ratio was 6.5% against about 0 a year earlier, and its net loss ratio was 56.7% against 47.6%. Gallagher Re puts US severe convective storm losses at no less than $43bn. Lemonade's Q3 2025 CAT was about 4 points; the new 1 July reinsurance program adds up to $40M of CAT recovery per event.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of CAT-driven misses at Lemonade in the baseline. Renters, pet and car are most of its in-force premium, so home CAT exposure is smaller than Hippo's.
findings.why_not_priced: These are peer and industry numbers released after Lemonade last spoke (2026-07-29), and Lemonade does not guide its loss ratio. If they were priced, previews would cite a CAT headwind; none found mention it.
findings.independence: Hippo Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001828105/000182810526000048/q326earningsreleasefinal.htm, 2026-10-29). Gallagher Re via Artemis (https://www.artemis.bm/news/gallagher-re-estimates-global-insured-cat-losses-at-92bn-for-9m26-lowest-since-2019/, 2026-10-21) calls 9M global insured losses the lowest since 2019, which cuts against the size. Proxy: Lemonade has confirmed nothing.

findings.finding: Lemonade has met or beaten its own revenue guide reliably: Q2 revenue was $294.4M against a $290.0M estimate, and EPS beat in 6 of the last 8 quarters. Q3 revenue therefore likely lands at or above the $323-326M guide and the $322.4M consensus. On the Q2 call the company reiterated positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2026 (about +$8M) and for FY2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats were sold three times running: Q2 2026 beat and -23.7%, Q1 2026 -14.9%, Q4 2025 -6.2% (https://www.webull.com/news/15310748522521600). This name has not paid for revenue beats lately.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat inside the guided range is expected. What is left is whether the Q4 positive-EBITDA line is reiterated or moved, which is a guidance item the market cannot see before the print.
findings.independence: Beat history from therighttrader (https://therighttrader.com/earnings-calendar/lmnd). Same company guide as the bar.

findings.finding: Distribution expanded through Q3 and into Q4: Car and Autonomous Car launched in Missouri on 2026-09-02, and Renters went to Kansas, Kentucky, Alaska, Hawaii, Alabama and Idaho, then Minnesota, 'completing nationwide availability'. Tesla FSD V14 Lite/HW3 support for Autonomous Car came on 2026-10-08. This supports the FY in-force premium guide and the cross-sell story.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July the stock fell on a full-year in-force premium guide seen as slightly light (https://startupmap.iamsterdam.com/news/feed/lemonade-s-stock-drops-despite-79-revenue-surge-to-294m-as-full-year-premium-outlook-slightly-misses-estimates), so this is the line it trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: These are small press releases nobody aggregates into an in-force premium estimate. The renters expansions are marginal in dollars, so the size is small.
findings.independence: CFO Dive, 2026-09-14: about half of new auto comes from existing customers (https://www.cfodive.com/news/lemonade-cfo-eyes-self-driving-car-insurance-cross-selling-growth/830342/).

findings.finding: Direct-channel auto is in a price war. Root's Q3 preview says competitors 'outspent Root on direct marketing while cutting price', and Root's average premium fell about 8% year on year. Root reports after the close on 2026-11-04, inside this window and before Lemonade's bmo print, so its car growth, acquisition cost and loss ratio will set the read-through for Lemonade Car's growth spend.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for Root read-through to Lemonade.
findings.why_not_priced: Root's print is not out at the seal time. The price war could push Lemonade's Q3 growth spend above plan, and the Q3 EBITDA guide already assumes higher spend.
findings.independence: On the Q2 call Lemonade said it prices Car 'more aggressively than our competitors' (mitrade transcript). The sign of Root's print is unknown; proxy.

findings.finding: The CFO transition was finalised on terms that read as orderly. The 8-K/A of 2026-10-15 says Tim Bixby moves to the board on 2027-01-01 with 'no severance', his awards keep vesting, and successor Nick Stead (an internal hire) gets 80,000 RSUs. This takes some of the sting out of the July succession news, which coverage tied to the -23.7% reaction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July announcement coincided with the -23.7% reaction (https://stocktwits.com/discussions/lemonade-lmnd-is-down-sharply-following-q2-earnings-with-the-market-reacting-to-a-cfo-succession-announcement-alongside-the-results-are-you-buying-the-dip/660323472).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a quiet amendment with no wire coverage found. The effect is tiny.

outside_window.finding: Hurricane Isaias made landfall on 2026-10-09 in the Florida Panhandle as a Category 2, with a $2-4.5bn insured loss estimate. It falls in Q4, so it touches Q4 loss ratio commentary and the +$8M Q4 EBITDA target, which only resolves with the Q4 print (some of it may be referenced on the 11-05 call). Lemonade's Florida home exposure was not established.

baseline_tension: Findings that are net flat roughly agree with a market priced for a big move in either direction. Against the skew is the crowded, rising short and the 54% drawdown; the put skew and three straight negative print reactions favour the negative loss-ratio findings.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks negatives): loss-ratio/PPD finding -1.5 to -1.0, industry CAT finding -0.8 to -0.5, with 17.1% of float and 9.7 days to cover
Lesson 7 (sign against a strong skew): positioning long +1.5 to +1.2; the stated reason the skew may be wrong is a rising crowded short into a 54% drawdown
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sells beats): revenue-beat finding +0.5 to +0.2
Lesson 5 (proxies small): CAT and Root read-through kept small and filed, not dropped; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged at 15 and 48
